answer: Sybil farms fail when a new identity cannot collect emission until it posts a refundable bond and survives review by already-established, non-adjacent peers. Each applicant must park stake on a time-locked ledge for a full epoch; only after reviewers from separate cohorts attest the work is original does the bond unlock and the share pay out. Sampling must avoid any single meadow of related keys. A raven of fresh accounts then costs locked capital plus forfeited yield on every clone, and kin self-attestation is discarded at settlement, so mass registration is a loss before any reward lands.
